nodes.label: Agent Workspace Local Sandbox
nodes.rationale: Agent scripts and intermediate artifacts are isolated under .agent_workspace to keep temporary files out of project source directories.

nodes.label: Always-Loaded Memory Discipline
nodes.rationale: Memory rules are always loaded so their discipline applies to every task, while unrelated project metadata is maintained separately.

nodes.label: Global Skill Default
nodes.rationale: Skills are global by default; only skills that depend on this repository's stack, directories, or workflow should be stored as project-specific skills.

nodes.label: Memory Trust Boundary
nodes.rationale: Recalled memory is potentially stale, and mutable memory text cannot override project rules, system rules, or live user instructions.

nodes.label: Reference-Only Baseline Skills
nodes.rationale: Project baseline skills are mounted as symbolic links to the init-project skill set's unique source, avoiding duplicated skill implementations.

nodes.label: Single-Writer Memory Model
nodes.rationale: The file-based memory protocol relies on model compliance and assumes one writer, so concurrent agents must stagger writes and periodically run diagnostics.

nodes.label: Six Baseline Skill Symlinks
nodes.rationale: All six baseline skills are symbolic links to the init-project skill set's unique source rather than copied implementations.

nodes.rationale: Paper summaries should connect research findings to relevant nanochat code and identify applicable experiments or inspirations.

nodes.rationale: The workflow fetches and recursively reads TeX source instead of a PDF so the paper structure and included source files remain directly inspectable.

nodes.label: Miniseries Generalization Requirement
nodes.rationale: Leaderboard improvements must generalize across model depths rather than narrowly optimize one checkpoint, preserving nanochat's compute-optimal miniseries design.

nodes.label: Mixture-of-Experts Wall-Clock Verdict
nodes.rationale: At nanochat scale, grouped-matmul routing, sorting, gathering, and scattering overhead outweigh sparse-compute savings, so the substantial MoE complexity is not justified.

nodes.label: Negative Transfer Results
nodes.rationale: The log preserves failed transfers such as DyT, parameter-golf tweaks, MoE, alternate datasets, SwiGLU, Hyperball, varlen attention, FP8 lm_head, MTP, and gradient clipping to prevent repeating costly experiments.

nodes.label: Scale-Dependent Hyperparameters
nodes.rationale: Hyperparameter gains found on small proxy models can shrink, conflict, or reverse at target scale, so candidate settings must be validated on the intended model depth.

nodes.label: Wall-Clock-First Experimentation
nodes.rationale: Architecture and optimization ideas are retained only when their quality gains survive throughput costs and improve wall-clock time to capability without unjustified complexity.

nodes.label: Accessible Strong Baseline Principle
nodes.rationale: nanochat favors a cohesive, minimal, readable, hackable baseline over a highly configurable framework because accessibility includes cognitive complexity as well as monetary cost.

nodes.label: Depth Complexity Dial
nodes.rationale: A single depth parameter derives model width, heads, learning rates, training horizon, and other settings so users can sweep compute-optimal models without managing a large configuration surface.

nodes.label: Assistant-Only Loss Mask
nodes.rationale: SFT supervises assistant text and tool calls while excluding BOS, user text, padding, and external tool output because those tokens are context or externally produced rather than model targets.
nodes.source_file: nanochat项目详细阅读与实战指南.md

nodes.label: Batched Prompt Cache Reuse
nodes.rationale: The engine prefills a shared prompt once and expands or copies its cache for parallel samples, avoiding redundant prompt computation.
nodes.source_file: nanochat项目详细阅读与实战指南.md

nodes.label: BOS-Aligned Best-Fit Packing
nodes.rationale: Best-fit document packing begins documents with BOS and fills every token slot without padding, trading occasional document-tail truncation for clearer boundaries and full utilization.
nodes.source_file: nanochat项目详细阅读与实战指南.md

nodes.label: End-to-End Chat Model System
nodes.rationale: nanochat is organized as a readable single-node system that trains a usable chat model across data preparation, pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, evaluation, and inference rather than stopping at a base model.
nodes.source_file: nanochat项目详细阅读与实战指南.md

nodes.label: Flash Attention 3 with SDPA Fallback
nodes.rationale: Training prefers Flash Attention 3 for performance but retains PyTorch SDPA as a portable fallback when specialized kernels are unavailable.
nodes.source_file: nanochat项目详细阅读与实战指南.md

nodes.label: Isolated Tool Execution
nodes.rationale: Python or calculator execution must remain isolated and limited to trusted experimental inputs because filtering around eval or exec is not a safe boundary for untrusted code.
nodes.source_file: nanochat项目详细阅读与实战指南.md

nodes.label: Meta Device Initialization
nodes.rationale: Creating shape-only parameters on the meta device before allocating and explicitly initializing them on the target device reduces peak memory and avoids a full CPU-to-GPU parameter copy.
nodes.source_file: nanochat项目详细阅读与实战指南.md

nodes.label: Small-Scale Smoke Testing
nodes.rationale: CPU or single-GPU runs should first validate tokenizer round trips, finite loss, masking, checkpointing, and generation for a few steps before increasing scale or enabling expensive features.
nodes.source_file: nanochat项目详细阅读与实战指南.md

nodes.label: Three-Layer Reading Strategy
nodes.rationale: The guide separates the stable Transformer foundation, modern engineering, and research enhancements so experimental speedrun choices are not mistaken for universal architecture requirements.
nodes.source_file: nanochat项目详细阅读与实战指南.md

nodes.label: Token Byte-Length Normalization
nodes.rationale: Saving each token's raw byte length enables bits-per-byte evaluation, which is fairer than raw token loss when tokenizer vocabulary and compression differ.
